raw_response:
Well, October's coming up fast, so I need to get my wheat sorted. I've farmed these 20 mu for 20 years now — since I was 21 — so I know the soil here pretty well. It's me and my wife handling the day-to-day; our two grown children work in a factory in town and only come back for harvest. That means we have to plan labor carefully. I can't do everything myself anymore, especially with that brutal week between wheat harvest and maize planting.

For wheat, I'll sow around October 8th if the weather holds. I'm buying Jinmai 47 seed this year — I saved my own seed last year, but after two years the vigor drops, so it's time for fresh seed. That's about 40 yuan per mu. I till the field with the rotary tiller first, then broadcast the seed and fertilizer together. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer and 15 kg of urea per mu as base. The extension agent keeps saying I should use less nitrogen, and my neighbor Wang tried 15 kg total last year and did okay, but two years ago when I cut back to 15 kg my wheat turned yellow at jointing and I lost yield. I'm not taking that risk again. At jointing in late March, I topdress another 20 kg of urea per mu. Total nitrogen is about 22 kg per mu — a bit high maybe, but I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than lose a big chunk of yield. I'd rather have cash for emergencies, but cutting fertilizer is where I don't save.

I irrigate wheat three times: overwintering in late November, jointing in March, and grain filling in May. Water costs 20 yuan per mu each time from the tube well, so that's 60 yuan per mu. I thought about skipping the overwintering irrigation to save money, but my uncle did that in 2019 and his wheat got winter-killed. Not worth it.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June — usually I have about five days. I hire two workers from the village for five days at 150 yuan per day each to help with harvest and planting. Without them, I'd never make the window. I plant 2.5 kg of hybrid maize seed per mu — I buy Jinong hybrid, costs about 70 yuan per mu. You can't save hybrid seed, so I buy every year. I put all the fertilizer down at planting: 40 kg compound plus 15 kg urea per mu. I know some people side-dress at the trumpet stage, but with double cropping I just don't have time to get back out here for that. I irrigate twice: once right after planting to get germination, and once at trumpet stage in early August. If we get good summer rain I might skip the second one, but I plan for two.

For chemicals, I spray herbicide once on each crop — spring for wheat, after emergence for maize. I also keep insecticide handy for maize; last year the corn borers were bad in the village, so I'll scout carefully.

My yield targets are 450 kg per mu for wheat and 500 kg per mu for maize. Last year was dry and I only got 400 kg wheat, but the soil moisture looks better this autumn. Total input cost is about 13,500 yuan. That's most of my cash reserves, but what else am I going to do? The land has to produce.

Wheat gets two fertilizer applications because I have time in the long growing season, and I push nitrogen a bit above what extension recommends because I got burned by under-application two years ago. Maize gets one shot at planting because the double-crop window is too tight for side-dressing. I hire labor for the harvest-planting crunch because missing that window costs more than the wages.
